name: Community Stewardship Grants (State NRM Program)

funder.name: Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development (Western Australia)

summary: Annual Western Australian Government grants for incorporated not-for-profit and community groups to protect and restore the local environment, from small projects to large strategic ones, with on-ground works such as revegetation, fencing and invasive species control.

amount.note: Small grants $1,000 to $50,000; large grants $50,001 to $450,000

eligibility.rule: Is an incorporated not-for-profit organisation with an ABN
Has a branch or base of operation in Western Australia
If holding State NRM grants, is up to date with their reporting and contracts
Is not a tertiary education institution
Is not a Western Australian or Australian Government agency
Project activities are additional to business as usual

documents: Signed Sponsorship Agreement, if applying under a sponsorship arrangement
Maps of on-ground activities, if relevant
Completed 2026 workplan in Microsoft Excel format
Letters of support or commitment from contributing organisations
Written landholder permissions for relevant properties

status.quote: Start Date: 12 March 2026 End Date: 29 April 2026 Status: Closed

opens.quote: Start Date: 12 March 2026 End Date: 29 April 2026 Status: Closed

deadline.quote: Start Date: 12 March 2026 End Date: 29 April 2026 Status: Closed

pool.quote: In 2026, $7 million in funding is available to support community-driven natural resource management projects across the state.

applicant_types.quote: Land Conservation District Committees local government authorities primary and secondary schools.

geography.quote: Projects must be based within the state of Western Australia.

access.quote: To be eligible to apply, applicants must be an incorporated not-for-profit organisation with an ABN.

window.quote: Community Stewardship Grants are available annually to support community-based projects that serve to protect and restore the local environment.

amount.quote: Small grants valued between $1,000 and $50,000 up to 18 months duration. Large grants valued between $50,001 and $450,000

effort.quote: All applications, together with any supporting documentation, must be submitted by 12 noon AWST on Wednesday 29 April 2026.
Initial assessment: each assessment panel member individually reviews each application; eligibility and compliance checks are undertaken
Panel convenes: all projects are assessed and prioritised by the panel as a group, seeking technical advice as required

eligibility.quote: To be eligible to apply, applicants must be an incorporated not-for-profit organisation with an ABN.
organisations that do not have a branch or base of operation in Western Australia

Applicants with existing State NRM Program grants must be up to date with all reporting and contractual requirements by the closing date of this grant round to be eligible to apply for new funds through the State NRM Program.
tertiary education institutions such as universities (government or privately funded), monotechnics, polytechnics or colleges
Western Australian or Australian Government agencies.
be in addition to business as usual.

documents.quote: Signed Sponsorship Agreement if the application is made under a sponsorship arrangement (see Section 6). • Maps of on-ground activities which show the detail of the works planned at each site and the landscape scale context across all sites, if relevant (see Section 8.5).

The workplan is an essential component of the application and must be completed in Microsoft Excel format using the new 2026 workplan template (see Section 8.6). • Letters of support/commitment: a letter or similar from each organisation that will cocontribute cash, other resources, or effort to the project that provides the details and value of what will be contributed (see Section 8.7).
Landholder permissions: written confirmation that access permission from all relevant land owners/managers has been obtained at the time of applying (see Section 8.8).
